title: Review of c26's held-out 240^2 predator test on fresh seeds 5 and 6: replicated, persistence 370 t and >= 700 t, one of two seeds >= 500 t again
summary: Same world and WORLD_P as the finding (PRED 1, T_INTRO 200, PSIG 8, DECB 0.002, DOMAIN 240), c26's own counter runle.py on seeds 5 and 6 to t=900, plus a labkit run of seed 5 (300 frames x 30 steps). Seed 5: one predator wave to 21 cells, prey down to 22, predator last seen at t=570 (370 t after introduction), prey back to 71 cells by t=900; labkit agrees (species B: 0 components at the end, mean 5.1, max 34; species A: 69 final, 62 persistent splits). Seed 6: predator waves to 25 cells cycling with prey between 24 and 57 cells; 7 predator cells remain at t=900, so persistence is >= 700 t (data/p240_s6.png). So on a fresh pair the same split appears, one run below and one above 500 t, as the finding's band reading says.

observations.finding: data/p240_s6.png: predator waves to t=900 (>= 700 t); data/p240_s5.png and rerun/seed5/FACTS.md: predator extinct at t=570 (370 t), prey recover to 69-71 cells

verdicts.limitation: Two more seeds at one size; the claim is a band of mixed outcomes, and four runs at 240^2 (two here, two in the finding) give 2 above and 2 below 500 t, which supports 'coin flip' but cannot fix the probability.
